label: E2F / DREAM targets
rationale: CDK4/6-cyclin D and CDK2-cyclin E phosphorylate RB; RB releases E2F and DREAM disassembles. CDK7 is the CAK that activates CDK1/2/4/6, so it feeds the same axis. Loss => E2F/DREAM targets down.

label: G2/M checkpoint
rationale: CDK2-cyclin A drives S->G2; the G2/M program is the downstream readout that separates CDK2 from CDK4/6.

label: short-half-life / P-TEFb-dependent
rationale: CDK9/P-TEFb releases paused Pol II; blocking pause release depletes short-half-life transcripts first (MYC, MCL1 are the canonical examples). CDK7 phosphorylates the CTD at Ser5 and feeds the same step.

label: MYC targets
rationale: the downstream consequence of depleting MYC itself.

label: long DDR genes
rationale: CDK12/13 suppress intronic polyadenylation; their loss truncates long, high-intron-density DDR genes and lowers full-length mRNA (Dubbury 2018; Krajewska 2019). The classic 'CDK12 loss = HR deficiency' signature.

label: DNA repair (Hallmark)
rationale: an independent, differently derived version of the same prediction.

label: interferon-gamma / STAT1 response
rationale: the Mediator kinase module phosphorylates STAT1 Ser727; CDK8/19 loss changes the interferon response. Direction is NOT pre-specified — the literature reports both, so this cell is tested two-sided and reported without a direction claim.

label: cholesterol / SREBP biosynthesis
rationale: CDK8 phosphorylates and destabilises nuclear SREBP-1c; CDK8 loss de-represses lipogenic and sterol genes (Zhao 2012).

label: translation / biosynthesis  (post-hoc)
rationale: the direction this dataset itself produced for CDK8 (`signatures.py`). Carried as a labelled comparator ONLY — it is not a prediction and cannot be reported as a confirmed one.
